newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU to take United States to WTO over Helms-Burton.
newsitem.headline: EU to take United States to WTO over Helms-Burton.

text.p: The European Union decided on Tuesday formally to escalate its dispute with the United States over anti-Cuba trade laws, agreeing to challenge Washington before the World Trade Organisation.
The General Affairs Council agreed to raise the complaint at the WTO, ending months of speculation over how far the EU was prepared to go to roll back the Helms-Burton Act.
An Irish presidency spokesman said the complaint would be filed on October 16.

The swiftness of the move came as something of a surprise as the EU had previously indicated that it would wait until after the November U.S. elections to make the move, hoping that negotiations in a post-election climate would prove easier.
"The view is that this is something that can't wait," an Irish EU presidency spokesman said. "EU interests need to be protected and prevaricating on it would only send a weak and indecisive signal."

He was speaking after the Council met in closed session to discuss opposition to the Helms-Burton Act, an amalgamation of years of anti-Cuba legislation, passed in July to a chorus of indignant opposition from some of Washington's strongest trade partners.

Among other things, the act allows naturalised Americans to sue in U.S. courts foreign companies or individuals deemed to have gained from investments in Cuban property confiscated since the communist revolution of 1959.

The EU has been considering a raft of retaliatory measures to the act and to the D'Amato Bill -- which seeks to outlaw trade with Iran and Libya -- and escalating a WTO dispute was considered a drastic, albeit dramatic last resort.
British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said that the question of whether or not the issue went to the WTO before the U.S. elections was largely irrelevant.
"I don't think that the question of elections in the United States...should determine European Union policy," he said.
Rifkind noted, however, that it would not be possible for a WTO panel to meet until after the elections despite the October complaint.
